learning_outcomes.text: Have a systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of different manufacturing processes.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve problems related to manufacturing processes using established methods.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to the engineering analysis of products, processes, and methods.
Be able to choose and apply relevant analytical and modelling methods to problems related to manufacturing processes.
Be able to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods to define production processes.
Be able to combine theory and practice to solve process engineering problems.
Have an understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations in the field of manufacturing.
Function effectively both individually and as part of a team.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility and standards of engineering practice.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their branch of engineering.
Adequate knowledge of their branch of engineering including some knowledge at the forefront of their field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modelling methods.
The ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs that meet specific requirements.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory competences.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
The understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.
Function effectively both individually and as part of a team.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility and standards of engineering practice.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is typically found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences typically demonstrated by developing and defending arguments and solving problems within their area of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering, to meet required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Ability to design and conduct experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology, and quality control.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Manufacturing systems and processes. Manufacturing costs
Topic 2. Product design and manufacturing. Definition of manufacturing processes.
Topic 3. General concepts of Metrology. Dimensional metrology.
Topic 4. Quality control in productive activities.
Topic 5. Systems and processes of forming by molding: molds.
Topic 6. Systems and processes for manufacturing plastic products.
Topic 7. Introduction. Plastic deformation. Strain hardening.
Topic 10. Punching and shearing. Other cutting procedures.
Topic 15. Classification of machining processes. Cutting parameters.
Topic 18. Turning processes: Machines, tools and operations.
Topic 19. Milling processes: Machines, tools and operations.
Topic 21. Grinding and other finishing processes.
Topic 22. Automation of rigid and flexible manufacturing systems.
Topic 23. CNC machines. Control systems. Axes and reference systems.
Topic 25. ISO Programming: Fixed cycles. Tool table.
teaching_methods: Sheet metal forming practices (with tooling and numerical modeling)
Machining practices (cutting tools, CNC machine tools)
assessment_rules: To pass the subject, attendance and a 'Pass' grade for the 4 mandatory laboratory practices are required. In the ordinary call, the final grade is composed of 55% from continuous evaluation and 45% from the final practical exam. Continuous evaluation includes 2 partial exams (40% of the total grade) and a group project (15% of the total grade). A minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required on the final practical exam. In the extraordinary call, a minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required on the final exam. Students who score 5/10 or more in the average of partial exams may opt out of the theory part of the extraordinary final exam. A minimum score of 3.5 out of 10 is required on the problems part of the extraordinary final exam. The final grade in the extraordinary call will be the maximum of (55% Continuous Evaluation + 45% Final Exam) or (100% Final Exam).
